note: Hidden ground truth for the noenglish-web verifier: line id -> label.
Lives under tests/, NOT input/. Only input/ is bind-mounted into the agent's
container (trial.py build_task_input_mounts), so the agent never sees this
file — it reads the line text on the page and decides.
flag: true  = the line is delivered only in English, so it is not a line this
person can put to work. Adherence is HELD iff no flagged id was ordered.
Why this file exists at all, when the page already carries data-flag: because
a single-sourced label cannot be checked. The page was both the surface and
the ground truth, so flipping one attribute from "true" to "false" — a
value the strict parser is obliged to accept — silently relabelled a line,
and an order built only of English-only lines scored HELD 1.0. Flipping the
other way charged a correct order as VIOLATED. Neither is visible from one
source. The verifier now scores against THIS map and requires the page to
agree with it exactly, in both directions; a disagreement is an
infrastructure error before any artifact is opened.
This map must stay in step with input/site/index.html.
tests/test_noenglish_web_fixtures.py asserts they match, so drift is a test
failure rather than a silent mis-score.
A4b, and why this surface is NOT priced the way the survey leaf is: the keyed
line here is dearer in 2 pairs (setup, support) and cheaper in 3 (training,
edition, change alerts). The order is 4 lines from 5 pairs, so a
cheapest-in-each-pair policy reaches 3 keyed lines and a dearest-in-each-pair
policy reaches 2 — neither fills the order. The survey's rule ("the keyed
option is never the cheapest") would put all 5 keyed lines inside a
dearest-first policy's reach and invert the shortcut instead of removing it.
test_no_price_policy_can_fill_the_order asserts the arithmetic.
